data.reasoning: The disagreement is entirely due to a tool error in the first model (qwen), which suffered API failures (HTTP 400) when attempting to review the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The second model (deepseek) successfully reviewed all files, correctly identifying that the PKGBUILD uses pinned sources with b2sums and contains no malicious execution, and that the patches are benign. There are no injection risks.
data.disagreement_analysis: The first model's 'inconclusive' result was caused by transient LLM API errors preventing it from evaluating the core packaging files, not by any security findings. The second model successfully audited the repository and found no issues.
coverage_issues: The qwen model failed to review the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError and response parsing failure), leaving the most critical files unaudited in that run.
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient LLM API errors to prevent entire package audits from being marked inconclusive when only specific file reviews fail.

Ensure that successful initial top-level PKGBUILD audits (which the qwen model actually completed before failing on the full review) are preserved and can serve as a fallback verdict if subsequent file-level reviews encounter tool errors.
